Select the ones you want to delete, then press the <Delete> key to send them to the Trash folder, or press <Shift+Delete> to delete them immediately, bypassing Trash.

You can use any of Thunderbird's search features to refine your selection.

content:
- go to TB menu > Settings > General > Language & Fonts > Fonts > click 'Advanced' button

- at the top, set 'Fonts for:' to Latin if it isn't already

- change Proportional and Monospace fonts/sizes to your liking

- set Minimum font size to 14, or lower if you want a small font size

- at the top, change set 'Fonts for:' to Other Writing Systems

- repeat the process of changing fonts/sizes

- at the bottom, make sure 'Allow messages to use other fonts' is disabled if desired > OK > close the popup

content: Thunderbird has been evolving for decades and will continue in that direction. It isn't just to be innovative; Thunderbird needs to change over time to support new directions by email providers and evolving protocols. This is everywhere; if you monitor email clients, then you are aware that both Mailbird and eM Client have just initiated their own new directions and expansion. Change happens everywhere. Businesses that use software as part of the business's workflow should go slowly when upgrading the software, whether it is Quickbooks or Thunderbird or other. Businesses need also to do routine backups, as glitches do happen, whether software or hardware. I might add that this forum is staffed by volunteers; we do not design the changes, nor do we write the code. We are users, the same as you. I share your concerns, but I believe our best strategy is to stay the course; Thunderbird keeps getting better, and coping with a bump here and there seems preferable to changing to a new course. There are just my personal comments. Was there a specific new feature that is your concern? Thank you.

content:
I do not know how to set the time zone used in the Date column of the Message List, but I did discover that upgrading my Thunderbird installation caused Thunderbird to start displaying the correct date/time in the Date column. It now matches the date/time displayed in the right of the message header pane.

I upgraded from Thunderbird 149.0 (desktop) to Thunderbird 153.6.0esr. After Thunderbird restarted, the date/times in the Date column were correct. Updating to Thunderbird 159 might also be effective.

I suspect that the cause of the difference was bug 2058419 "Update to tzdata2026e". I interpret tzdata2026e to be a recent 2026-vintage bundle of time zone definitions, including the correct definition for the America/Vancouver time zone to which my operating system is set.
